Released on Sept. 12, 2006, Mayer’s third studio album builds a world of introspective lyricism that grapples with the idea of the passage of time, weaves between reality and a dream-like state and touches upon some of the political discourse of a post-September 11 world — but at its core, it’s a heartbreak album. Written and produced before his dating life reached a boiling point in the tabloids during the mid-’00s, Mayer waded through the different stages of grief in the grooviest way possible on Continuum . From denial to anger, bargaining, depression and acceptance, Mayer brought the listener one step further with plans for his future relationships. title: Here’s Why All 5 Variety Series Nominees Could Win at the 2026 Primetime Emmys
summary: It could be a long segment, but at least it should be funny.
body: If you’re planning to watch the 2026 Primetime Emmys on Monday (Sept. 14), brace yourself for a long (but likely highly entertaining) segment when they hand out the award for outstanding variety series. Thanks to a rule change this year, there could be multiple winners in that category. Beginning this year, the Television Academy combined best scripted variety series and best talk series into a single category: best variety series. The academy also converted it to what they call “an area award,” which means the nominees aren’t directly competing against each other. Instead, voters answer one question for each nominated show: “Does this nominee merit an Emmy?” Any series that receives at least 90% “yes” votes is awarded an Emmy. (If no nominee meets that threshold, the show with the highest approval percentage takes the trophy.) All the nominees are worthy and could very well clear that bar: The Daily Show (Comedy Central), Jimmy Kimmel Live! title: Meta’s Project Phoenix just leaked, and it looks nothing like a Quest
summary: Project Phoenix looks ready to make bulky headsets feel very yesterday.
body: TL;DR Images found inside Meta’s HorizonOS Prescription Lens app appear to reveal the rumored Project Phoenix headset ahead of Meta Connect on September 23. Phoenix looks more like chunky glasses than a traditional Quest headset, with glasses-style nose pads, sensors around the temples, and a separate compute puck. We still haven’t seen Phoenix properly from the front or on someone’s face, leaving big questions about its size, appearance, and overall design. Meta Connect kicks off on September 23, and we may have just gotten an early peek at one of the more interesting devices Meta could be preparing to talk about. UploadVR has spotted images of Meta’s rumored Project Phoenix headset inside the HorizonOS Prescription Lens app. While they don’t show the full device, they reveal enough to suggest Phoenix won’t be another Quest-style headset . Instead, Meta appears to be going for something much slimmer. From the angles shown, Phoenix looks more like chunky glasses than a conventional VR headset. Nose pads hold the device in place, while what appear to be sensors sit around the temples. The overall look immediately reminds me of XREAL Aura glasses , which use a similar setup.

Major Two galaxies merge at a furious rate in this Aug. 25, 2026, image of the II Zw 096 system. This and several other images of both visually and scientifically interesting galaxies were released by NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes. Chandra X-ray data (magenta) pinpoint powerful black hole activity and hot gas, while optical data (blue and white) from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and infrared data from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope illuminate vast stellar nurseries hidden behind interstellar dust. Systems like II Zw 096 show us how powerful galaxy collisions shaped the early universe. See more galaxy photos from Chandra. title: Survey uncovers the Pixel series’ biggest connectivity weakness, and it’s not slow mobile data
summary: Efficiency continues to plague Pixels, but can the Pixel 11 set things right?
body: Google Pixels are generally regarded as pretty reliable Android phones. I’d certainly recommend them to friends and family craving a solid Android experience. However, they do have a few chinks in their armor, and one that seems to cause repeated problems is a lackluster connectivity experience. Older Pixels have had notable modem-related flaws, from the Pixel 6’s reception problems through to the Pixel 10’s more recent Wi-Fi and Bluetooth woes . Thankfully, that’s something Google has seemingly acknowledged and is now addressing by switching to MediaTek modems. However, we were certainly intrigued to learn exactly which connectivity issues Pixel users have suffered from in the past.

title: I tried out the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Google still can’t convince me to buy a foldable
summary: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is better than ever. But is it finally worth it? Ehh...
body: It’s been a while since I last used a book-style foldable . My previous dalliance was the OPPO Find N2 back in 2022, and while I was impressed by how far the form factor had already come, I ultimately didn’t see enough reason to make the switch. Like many other potential converts, the drawbacks simply weren’t worth the small benefits. Four years on, I’m back to find out whether things have finally changed with the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold. I’ve spent plenty of time with Pixel Pro flagships in the intervening years and have generally been a fan of Google’s software, cameras, and even some of its latest AI-focused approaches. But does that familiar Pixel formula work when you double the screen and fold the whole thing in half? More importantly, has the foldable finally become something I actually want to use every day?

title: 5 Android phones you should buy instead of the Google Pixel 11 Pro
summary: Google has plenty of competition.
body: The Pixel 11 Pro is precisely what I thought it would be, and it’s still been as divisive as ever. Early reviews have been positive, and it’s clear Google leaned into what has made its Pixel lineup more successful over the last few years. The phones are pleasant and easy to use, ideal for beginners switching over to Android for the first time. However, it’s also never been more apparent that Pixels aren’t for enthusiasts who stare at benchmarks before buying a phone. And the Pixel 11 Pro has legitimate weaknesses. It’s fair to point them out and explain that people may want alternatives.

title: The iPhone 18 Pro camera is already years behind 2026 Android phones
summary: The iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture camera sounds impressive, but it's not enough for me.
body: Much of this week’s talk about Apple’s new releases centers on the brand’s first foldable—the iPhone Duo . But as a practical individual, I imagine a lot more consumers will be looking at the iPhone 18 Pro series and pondering whether there’s enough new hardware to justify the price hikes. While there are some key tweaks to processing power and new camera software tools, the iPhone’s latest innovation is a return to variable-aperture technology, ranging from f/1.48 to f/4, that Android rivals trialed and abandoned years ago. If this is seriously the best Apple can do to catch up with China’s best camera phones, I can’t see serious photographers like myself rushing to switch to the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max.

title: 8 iPhone Duo features every Android foldable needs to copy in 2027
summary: Apple's first foldable gets a surprising number of things right.
body: It’s no longer a dream. Apple officially makes foldable phones now. The company unveiled its first foldable iPhone , the iPhone Duo, at its September 9 event at Apple Park, finally entering a category that Samsung, Motorola, Google, and other Android manufacturers have competed in for years. But in typical Apple fashion, the company hasn’t simply launched another foldable phone. Apple has taken a form factor that’s been around for nearly a decade, looked at some of the problems we’ve almost learned to live with, and introduced a few interesting solutions of its own. And now I want Samsung, Google, and Motorola to copy these iPhone Duo features for their next foldables.

title: Your Pixel phone quietly got a new feature to help prevent motion sickness — here’s how to use it
summary: Motion Assist to save the day.
body: Motion sickness is not a fun thing to deal with. While I don’t personally struggle with it, I’ve known people who do, and it seems like it can be pretty unbearable at times. Thankfully, if you have a Pixel phone, you now have a clever new feature that can help keep motion sickness at bay. The feature is called “ Motion Assist ,” and it works by displaying small dots around the edge of your screen that move according to your phone’s gyroscope and accelerometer. So, if you’re riding in a car, the dots will follow the same motion/movement as the vehicle.

title: Android just made switching password managers a whole lot safer and easier
summary: Your passwords finally get a safer ride to their new home.
body: TL;DR Android is making it easier and safer to move passwords and passkeys between supported password managers. The new system removes the need to export your password vault as a potentially unencrypted file and manually import it elsewhere. Password transfers currently work with Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden, and Dashlane, with more services coming later. Passwords are basically the keys to our digital lives. They protect everything from our emails and social media accounts to banking apps and personal photos, so the last thing you want is to accidentally leave them exposed. Unfortunately, that can become a concern when you decide to switch password managers. Right now, you may have to export your entire vault as a file, save it to your device, and then import it into your new password manager . Worse, that exported file can be unencrypted, which means all those usernames and passwords you’ve spent years protecting could temporarily sit together in a regular file on your phone. You also have to remember to delete it once you’re done.

title: Fixing the Fold 8’s flawed stereo speaker was this easy? iPhone Duo shows the way
summary: Better speaker placement is only the beginning of Samsung’s headache.
body: TL;DR The Galaxy Z Fold 8 places both speakers on one side, reducing stereo separation when the phone is unfolded in landscape orientation. Apple puts the iPhone Duo’s speakers on opposite halves diagonally, creating a more balanced layout for videos, games, and music. Apple’s first foldable also beats Samsung’s eighth-generation model in several other areas, despite costing only slightly more. Samsung has spent seven years refining book-style foldables, so its $2,000 Galaxy Z Fold 8 should represent the category at its most mature. At that price, buyers should not have to excuse obvious compromises as quirks of the form factor. Yet Apple has entered the foldable race with the iPhone Duo and, on its first attempt, addressed several limitations Samsung still expects Fold buyers to accept and live with. One clear example is speaker placement. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has two speakers, but Samsung placed both in the half housing the cover display. That arrangement works as expected when watching something on the outer screen in landscape orientation, with a speaker firing from either side.

title: Apple’s new Watch outpaces the Pixel Watch 4 for heart rate accuracy, but its real rival is missing
summary: Google’s older wearable still delivered a few surprises in Apple’s study.
body: TL;DR Apple’s large-scale study found the Watch Series 12 more accurate than the Pixel Watch 4 overall for heart-rate tracking. The Pixel Watch 4 matched Apple during cycling and narrowly beat it at rest under two accuracy measures. The newer Pixel Watch 5 and Galaxy Watch 9 missed the test because Apple selected competitors available by June. The Pixel Watch has spent generations closing the health and fitness gap with established wearables, even becoming a strong Apple Watch alternative for Android users. Apple has now fired back with a heart-rate accuracy study that puts its Series 12 ahead of the Pixel Watch 4 — although Google’s current Pixel Watch 5 never got to compete. Apple says the Watch Series 12 recorded significantly lower overall heart rate error than every tested rival across workouts and everyday activities. Despite losing the overall contest, the Pixel Watch 4 was among Apple’s closest smartwatch challengers in several measurements. The two watches were statistically inseparable during outdoor cycling under the study’s main Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) calculations.

title: Why RayNeo is the only AR eyewear company you can bet on
summary: From personal theater displays to invisible-screen eyewear, RayNeo's three AR glasses target real-world use cases.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority From virtual movie screens anywhere to real-time information without reaching for your phone, smart glasses have come a long way. The best models now pack sharp built-in displays, hands-free AI assistants, and hardware light enough to wear all day, features that felt like science fiction only a couple of product cycles ago. The one thing still holding a lot of these companies back, though, is staying power. Plenty of smart glasses makers build around a single standout product, and when consumer interest shifts, there’s no easy alternative. RayNeo is taking a different route, and the numbers back it up. The company is #1 in global AR glasses shipments for the first half of 2026, and its RayNeo Air 4 Series led global AR glasses sales volume outright and was the best seller during Amazon Prime Day 2026. That kind of shipment dominance comes from three distinct lines that cover the smart glasses spectrum: a top-tier display line built for cinematic viewing and travel, camera-free ambient AI eyewear you wear all day, and a full standalone AR computer for developers and creators. Here’s what you need to know.

title: Is gaming on the Pixel 11 really that bad? I played 3 popular games to find out
summary: Last-gen performance wouldn't be so bad, if Tensor wasn't already years out of date.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority The Tensor G6 chip in Google’s Pixel 11 series is off to a not-so-great start. First, the chip’s benchmarks are notably behind the competition, which is pretty much par for the course. Then, during launch week, gamers saw graphical glitches in popular titles like Genshin Impact — prompting fears of a redux of last year’s driver issues that plagued the Pixel 10’s Tensor G5 chip for months. However, are things really that bad? To put it to the test, I played my usual assortment of popular Android games, recording frame rate, temperatures, and power draw data. For the test, I booted up Call of Duty Mobile’s Battle Royale mode, the fast-paced Asphalt Legends racing game, and the ever-demanding Genshin Impact. I turned the settings up as high as my Pixel 11 Pro XL would let me: medium settings with a 90fps limit in COD, high settings with a 60fps limit in Asphalt Legends, and high/max settings with a similar 60fps cap in Genshin Impact.

Another quarterly update could arrive in October, although Samsung has not acknowledged the problems or promised a fix. The Galaxy A07 4G is the best-selling budget Android phone this year , and its software support is one of its biggest selling points. It launched with Android 15 and is eligible for six major Android OS upgrades. The Galaxy A07 5G variant arrived with Android 16 out of the box, and both models have since moved to One UI 8.5 . Unfortunately, that generous update promise is now colliding with the other side of long-term support: software that appears to have made everyday use worse for some owners. Reports across Reddit , Facebook , and Samsung’s community forums describe persistent lag and touchscreen problems after installing One UI 8.5. Complaints include general stuttering and touch input that suddenly freezes or takes unusually long to register .

title: Motorola shows off its new wide foldable in swipe at Apple
summary: The future is wide.
body: TL;DR Motorola has teased a new folding phone with proportions similar to Apple’s new iPhone Duo. The phone previously leaked last week in the form of sketches. We expect Moto’s wider foldable will be announced in the months ahead. Apple announced a bunch of new stuff today: the iPhone 18 Pro , new AirPods , new Apple Watches, and its first-ever folding phone, the iPhone Duo . Based on the favorable look Apple’s given us at it so far, the Duo seems pretty great. But there’s no denying Apple is years late to the party, and Motorola’s having some fun with that at Apple’s expense.
